claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into both operands of every SqlBinaryExpression with no operator filter, so operands under AndAlso/OrElse/Coalesce (which do not propagate NULL) enter the set and their IS NOT NULL guard is deleted, returning wrong data.
raw:
### C1 — `NullPropagatedOperands` recurses into every binary operator, including ones that do not propagate NULL
`SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:626-630`

```csharp
else if (expression is SqlBinaryExpression binary)   // no operator filter
```

`SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator` ... admits `AndAlso`, `OrElse`, and `Coalesce`, none of which propagate NULL

claim: The unsound rewrite corrupts filtering as well as projection: a Where over a null-propagating ternary becomes WHERE NA <> NB OR NB IS NULL and returns an extra row that must be excluded.
raw: **It also corrupts filtering, not just projection.** `Where(x => (x.NA != null ? (bool?)(x.NA != x.NB) : null) == true)` becomes `WHERE NA <> NB OR NB IS NULL` and returns **row Id=1 (`NA=NULL, NB=NULL`), which must be excluded** — expected `[4]`, got `[1, 4]`.

claim: Coalesce is claimed to be safe only by accident because SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce emits a SqlFunctionExpression the function arm skips, but the tested verdict is that it does not currently regress.
raw: `Coalesce` is currently safe only by accident — `SqlExpressionFactory.Coalesce` (`SqlExpressionFactory.cs:485-511`) emits a `SqlFunctionExpression` with `argumentsPropagateNullability: [false, false]`, which the function arm correctly skips. Verified: it does not regress. But the type permits `SqlBinaryExpression{Coalesce}`, so this is one refactor ... away from live.

claim: On SQL Server the optimization is wrong even for null-propagating operators, because SearchConditionConvertingExpressionVisitor runs after nullability processing and wraps the bare predicate in a two-arm CASE that collapses UNKNOWN to false, destroying the NULL the dropped outer guard preserved.
raw:
### C2 — On SQL Server the optimization is wrong even for operators that *do* propagate NULL
`SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:576-591`

This is a second, independent defect ... afterwards `ConvertToValue` ... wraps it as `CASE WHEN <pred> THEN true ELSE false END`. That collapses `UNKNOWN` into **false**, destroying the NULL the outer guard used to preserve.

claim: The WHEN result is deliberately specialized using the test's non-nullable-column knowledge (producing A = B AND B IS NOT NULL), and the new optimizer walks through that AndAlso and deletes the very guard the specialization was predicated on, invalidating its own premise.
raw:
### C3 — The result is specialized under the very test being deleted
`SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:512-514` interacting with `:576-591`

... `A == B` is specialized to `A = B AND B IS NOT NULL` — an `AndAlso` whose right arm exists *precisely* to convert `UNKNOWN` to `FALSE` under the guard. The new code then walks through that `AndAlso`, finds `A`, and deletes the guard

claim: The optimization block never consults allowOptimizedExpansion, so it cannot distinguish a predicate context (where NULL to false is licensed) from a projection (where it is not).
raw: Related: the block at `:578` never consults `allowOptimizedExpansion`, so it cannot distinguish a predicate context (where NULL→false is licensed) from a projection (where it is not).

claim: The dependency between the test-driven result specialization and the new optimization is nowhere documented, so a future editor of the specialization has no way to know they can break the optimizer.
raw: It is also nowhere documented, so the next person editing `:512` has no way to know they can break `:583`.

claim: The new code uses func.Instance! with only an InstancePropagatesNullability check, dropping the Instance: not null half that line 2394 of the same file already guards, so a provider constructing instance null with instancePropagatesNullability true would cause an NRE during query compilation.
raw:
### I1 — `func.Instance!` contradicts the established pattern in this same file
`SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:633-636` ... nothing rejects `instance: null, instancePropagatesNullability: true`. Line 2394 ... already guards correctly:

```csharp
if (sqlFunctionExpression is { Instance: not null, InstancePropagatesNullability: true })
```

claim: All five new tests project int? or string and not one projects a bool?, which is exactly where every reproduced failure lives, so the added tests are structurally incapable of catching this bug class.
raw:
### I2 — The tests are structurally incapable of catching this bug class
`NullSemanticsQueryTestBase.cs:2250-2294`

All five new tests project `int?` or `string`. **Not one projects a `bool?`** — which is where every failure above lives. ... a single added test would have failed loudly at authoring time:

`x => x.NullableBoolA != null ? (bool?)(x.NullableBoolA != x.NullableBoolB) : null`

claim: Select_null_propagation_negative1/2 appear to cover this case but do not, because they use a different column in the guard than in the result so nothing can match the hash set, and the PR adds zero negative tests.
raw: The existing `Select_null_propagation_negative1/2` (`test/EFCore.SqlServer.FunctionalTests/Query/GearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs:1074, :1091`) look like they cover this but do not — they use a *different* column in the guard than in the result, so nothing can match the hash set. The PR adds zero negative tests.

claim: Three new branches are untested: the InstancePropagatesNullability branch, the niladic guard, and the right is null then left arm.
raw: Also untested: the `InstancePropagatesNullability` branch (`:633-636`, only reachable via spatial/hierarchyid providers), the niladic guard (`:638`), and the `right is null ? left` arm (`:608`).

claim: The no-ELSE form CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN x END is semantically identical to ELSE NULL but never optimizes; the guard should widen to (elseResult is null || IsNull(elseResult)).
raw: - **Missed optimization — no-`ELSE` form skipped.** `src/EFCore.Relational/Query/SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:578`. `IsNull(null)` is `false` (`:1633`), so `CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN x END` — semantically identical to `ELSE NULL`, and acknowledged as such at `:562` and `:573` — never optimizes. Widen to `(elseResult is null || IsNull(elseResult))`.

claim: Using null to mean TRUE inverts the local convention where a null SqlExpression? means absent, rests entirely on a two-character comment, and ignores the file's canonical IsTrue/Constant(true) encoding.
raw: - **`null`-means-TRUE sentinel is undocumented and inverts local convention.** `:595`, `:600`, `:585`. Everywhere else in this method a null `SqlExpression?` means *absent* ... The entire contract rests on the two-character comment `// true`. The file already has a canonical encoding (`IsTrue`/`Constant(true)`, used at `:521-532`).

claim: Nine stale // issue #16050 markers remain on baselines whose SQL this PR made optimal, across GearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest, TPTGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest, and TPCGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.
raw: - **9 stale `// issue #16050` comments.** The marker flags known-suboptimal baselines; this PR made the SQL beneath these optimal but left the comments: `GearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs:1018, :1031, :1044`; `TPTGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs:1231, :1247, :1263`; `TPCGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs:1410, :1429, :1448`. Still valid for `optimization2/3/4`.

claim: NullPropagatedOperands is a noun phrase on a void procedure while every sibling helper is a verb, and its tense reads backwards relative to EF's own ArgumentsPropagateNullability; CollectNullPropagatingOperands would be clearer.
raw: - **Naming and structure.** `NullPropagatedOperands` (`:617`) is a noun phrase on a `void` procedure — every sibling helper is a verb (`DropNotNullChecks`, `TryMakeNonNullable`, `AddNonNullableColumn`). The tense is also backwards ... Reversing that reading is precisely the C1 bug. `CollectNullPropagatingOperands` would be clearer.

claim: Inserting every traversed subtree into a HashSet<SqlExpression> costs O(n^2) on the query-compilation path because no SqlExpression caches its hash code, and the set is built before it is known to be needed.
raw: - **O(n²) hashing on the compilation path.** `:619` inserts every traversed subtree into a `HashSet<SqlExpression>`, and no `SqlExpression` caches its hash code ... Inserting an *n*-node result costs O(n²). Walking the test's 1-3 conjuncts against the result would be O(t·n) and allocation-free. The set is also built before it is known to be needed.

claim: RestoreNullValueColumnsList is passed currentNonNullableColumnsCount where currentNullValueColumnsCount is intended, but git blame dates it to 2023 so it is explicitly declared pre-existing and out of scope for this diff.
raw:
## Adjacent, out of scope

`SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:539` passes `currentNonNullableColumnsCount` to `RestoreNullValueColumnsList` where `currentNullValueColumnsCount` is intended (compare the correct pairing at `:528-529`). `git blame` dates it to 2023-10-23 — **pre-existing, not this diff**

claim: IsNull also matches a null-valued SqlParameterExpression, which would make the rewrite parameter-value-dependent, but the claim was withheld as unreachable because VisitSqlParameter rewrites null-valued parameters into null constants first.
raw: **One claim I'm glad I left out.** `IsNull` (`:1633`) also matches a null-valued `SqlParameterExpression`, which would make this a parameter-value-dependent rewrite. It isn't reachable here — `VisitSqlParameter` (`:1552-1562`) rewrites null-valued parameters into null constants before `IsNull` ever sees one on this path.

raw: Two notes on method: the repo's test projects do not compile under the installed SDK 10.0.203 (`test/EFCore.Specification.Tests/CustomConvertersTestBase.cs:1202`, CS0023 — pre-existing, unrelated to this diff), so all reproduction ran from standalone apps in `/tmp` project-referencing `src/`.
